newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian light crude premiums firm, Oman steady.
newsitem.headline: Asian light crude premiums firm, Oman steady.

text.p: Cash crude premiums in Asia were mixed on Friday with light sweet grades supported by firmer Tapis premiums and Oman holding recent levels.
Traders said a partial Tapis cargo for second half February traded at a premium of $1.75 over published quotes, five cents higher than the last deal and reflecting the continued firm trend for Tapis.

February Tapis swaps were quoted at $25.25/$25.35 per barrel -- down 25 cent on the day -- with 200,000 paper barrels changing hands between a U.S. trader and a Swiss-based trader at $25.35 per barrel.
That left outright prices for February at $27.10.
The weaker tone of swaps was attributed to overnight Brent and NYMEX losses, but otherwise there was general support for Tapis because from winter demand and good refinery margins.
But published weekly quotes -- on which the swaps market is based -- jumped 85 cents this week to $26.18.
The Swiss-trader was heard buying 150,000 barrels of March paper Tapis at $24.58 and also balance January paper at $26.02.
Two majors were heard making enquiries for first half light sweet February barrels because of difficulties with the loss of production from the Cossack and Griffin fields in Australia.
Cossack was expected back up Friday and Griffin was monitoring the sea states after the latest cyclone.
Various Oman cargoes were heard sold by the Oman government. The Oman refinery is down for maintenance in March, so the government was five cargoes extra to sell.

One was heard sold Friday to a European major at MPM +27/29, another to a Japanese trader at MPM +27/29 and a third to another Japanese trader at MPM +29 cents. The deals maintained the generally firm level for Oman crude.
